narrative.title: Decoding the Engraver's Numeral Bands
narrative.scenario: A heritage engraving workshop receives restoration orders whose dates are carved as Roman numeral bands, and the CNC controller needs plain integers before it can program a job. The shop follows the standard convention: a smaller symbol placed before a larger one is subtractive, everything else adds up. The controller parses the band left to right, adding symbol values and flipping to subtraction whenever a smaller symbol precedes a larger.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s representing a Roman numeral, using the symbols I, V, X, L, C, D and M.
narrative.outputFormat: The integer value the numeral denotes.
constraints: s is guaranteed to be a valid Roman numeral in the range [1, 3999]

testCases.explanation: Three additive I symbols, no subtractive pairs.
L is 50, V is 5 and III is 3; no symbol precedes a larger one, so everything adds.

hintLevels: Level 1: Every symbol has a fixed value; the only wrinkle is a smaller value standing just before a bigger one.
Level 2: Scan left to right — add the current symbol's value, but subtract it instead when the next symbol is larger.
Level 3: The subtractive pairs are exactly IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM; equivalently, subtract when value[i] < value[i+1] — and don't forget the final symbol still adds.
